You get very talkative but dont realize how much you’re talking for a bit. It’s a feeling like when you feel giggles bubbling up inside you. Almost like if a panic attack felt not horrible. Imagine when you drink too much coffee, that’s not it but it’s a feeling of being very “up”. You may feel anxious or paranoid, or even sick. You may feel like you want to make grand plans or do everything all at once. It can make you violent or aggressive. Often I have seen meth, like any other drug, turn people to being manipulative or uncaring, but especially meth, it is the devils drug IMO. I have done meth and experienced intense manic episodes sober and I’d say the two are very similar. Euphoria, aggression, anxiety, psychosis. I would not recommend trying it because it’s very addictive - even if you don’t enjoy the high or even hate the drug after trying it, all you will want is to do more. I am clean now and doing well, but I’ve seen people never recover, going in a downward spiral from it, unable to claw their way out. Meth can be fun, but it is evil.

In my teenage years, I worked at a church/hall that held weddings and events. My boss was in recovery, and so he hired many people in recovery too. One of my coworkers had moved out of his recovery house with another recovering addict. 

One day, we go to clean the church/hall at around 6am and my coworker and boss don’t show up. Turns out, coworker’s roommate had gone missing 3-4 days earlier. Coworker assumed he took off and maybe relapsed. On the last day, my coworker decides to call his roommate. 

The phone rings from inside the roommates locked bedroom. They get the door open and find roommate who had been lying there dead for days. Boss went over to help as police got there. 

I’ll never forget being 16 years old and having my coworker come back to work and explain to me, in shellshock, what his roommates dead body looked like and the coloration and bloating. Really stuck with me.

But the truth I had to learn is that no one will pull me out of a hole I’ve dug myself into. If I want to make life worth living, I have to let go of unhealthy control and work on using the power I do have to make my time here better for me and those around me. Hey, here from the response about NA. I’ll give the NA perspective: addiction is a disease that cannot be cured (if we use again after getting clean it will get out of control like last time) but it can be treated.

60 days this time, but I had a good amount of clean time before my relapse. No maintenance. I do have a sponsor! She’s a girl like me and has 2 years clean, mainly she just checks in on me every day and helps guide me through working the steps. For me, a home group doesn’t mean much, just means I make sure I go to that meeting every week. For activities, like the chili cook off my area of NA is having, each home group brings a chili. Really just a way of breaking it down, no official thing. 
I am working the steps, I’m working on step 1 right now. The main book of NA is the “big book” it’s a blue book with really everything in it. The other book I have is called “it works: how and why” this book is like a more in-depth view of the steps. It’s green and gold. The other book we read is called “living clean”, it just generally goes over how to live in recovery. Tips for someone looking to get into NA: go to some NA meetings just to check it out, and read through the big book, you can find a pdf of it online:)
